description: Connect pressed on the Control UI's OWN login gate, the upstream page's 'Gateway unreachable' screen with its Connect button, and that gate's own presence. This file is the ONE owner of the selectors that name that gate, the reports the page produces about it, how long a client holds its loading cover for one, and the injected script that watches for both the gate and the press. core/login-gate-connect.js reads it for the desktop, and the iOS client bundles this file and installs the same script.
why: Reported from the macOS desktop build 1.0.1-dev.358 (Abi, 2026-09-25): "when we get sent back to the can't connect to gateway error from the control UI when we hit connect it just hangs there for a while, we should do the load page there until the UI renders". The screen is the Control UI's own: a reconnect of ours loads the page, the page's socket is refused, and the page draws its login gate with a network failure. Pressing its Connect pins the gate on screen while the page connects (app-root.ts, loginGatePinned), and the gate then sits there, unchanged, for as long as the attempt takes. Measured with desktop/scripts/test-login-gate-connect.js against a real gateway: the gate with nothing moving for the whole of a four-second connect.

The reader never sees that screen at all (Abi, 2026-09-25: "if we never show the control UIs own connection screen that would be ideal, control the whole auth flow"). The gate is the Control UI's own answer to 'this client is not connected', and a client with no connection shows one of ITS OWN surfaces rather than a gateway page (core/ui/CONVENTIONS.md, the second rule): the loading cover in its failed state with Try again, the path a failed launch takes, and the app's own settings are where the reader changes the gateway or its token. So the script reports the gate's arrival and departure too, and while it is up the cover is held and then failed rather than lifted onto it.

A gate that is up says the page is NOT connecting (the Control UI draws it only when it has given up), so the cover is not kept waiting for something more: gateMs is the whole of the wait, and it is short for that reason. page-ready is the reset rather than an ending, because a gate reported by one document says nothing about the next one, and without it a gate that was up when a new page began would hold the cover down over a page that is connecting normally.

The page is upstream's and is not patched. Nothing here changes what the press does: the script listens in the capture phase and only REPORTS, so the page's own handler runs exactly as before, and a client that never installs this sees the page behave as it always did.

The press rather than the socket. A socket opened while the gate is up is almost always the press, but the gate's own Connect is the one signal that is certainly the reader's, and the Enter key in its fields is the same submission (login-gate.ts calls onConnect for both). Reading the socket instead would also cover a page that retried on its own, which is a cover nobody asked for.

Rendered means the gate has GONE, not that the socket opened. The page connects and only then replaces the gate with the interface, so the report waits for the gate to leave the document and then two animation frames, the same presented-frame rule core/spec/render-ready.json uses for a load. The two frames are bounded at 250ms, because iOS gives no frames to a web view under a cover it treats as hidden, and a report waiting on one never came: measured on the simulator, the cover sat until the deadline over an interface that had already replaced the gate.

A failure is the gate's failure callout coming BACK. The press clears the previous failure while the attempt runs, so a callout still on screen at the moment of the press is the old one; only one that returns after it has gone is this attempt's answer. Its title travels with the report so the client's failure notice can say what the page said.

deadlineMs bounds the whole thing, because a watcher that can only succeed is a cover that never lets go (core/ui/CONVENTIONS.md). A press with no answer by then lands on the loading cover's failed state with Try again, the path a failed launch takes. The script stops watching at the same moment, so a late answer cannot lift a cover the client has already failed.

The reports travel on the pairing observer's channel (clawPairing on iOS, the __clawPairing global on the desktop) rather than a new one, because it is already the one thing the gateway page may say to this app, and a second channel would be a second surface for the page to reach.

The selectors are upstream's names (ui/src/components/login-gate.ts), so a rename upstream would make the press invisible and the old hang would come back without an error. core/test/login-gate-connect.test.js checks them against the OpenClaw checkout when it is readable.
hook: if (node && node.nodeType === 1 && typeof node.matches === 'function' && node.matches(selector)) return true;
// The gate itself, and the document it is in. A page sitting on its own login
// gate is never revealed: the reader's surface for a client that is not
// connected is the loading cover's failed state (core/ui/CONVENTIONS.md).
var text = node && typeof node.textContent === 'string' ? node.textContent.trim().slice(0, 160) : '';
try { new MutationObserver(reportGate).observe(document, { subtree: true, childList: true }); } catch (e) {}
// One press at a time. The watch ends on the first answer, or quietly once the
// host's own deadline has passed, and the host owns what happens then.
// The gate has gone, so the interface is being drawn in its place. Two
// frames, so the frame that carries it has been presented before we say so,
// or a short bound: a web view under a cover may not be given frames at all
// (iOS stops them for a view it treats as hidden), and a report that waits
// on a frame that never comes is a cover that never lifts.
var say = function () { if (said) return; said = true; post({ kind: 'connect-rendered' }); };
// A press clears the gate's previous failure while the attempt runs, so a
// failure is only this attempt's once the old one has been seen to go.
var title = titleNode && typeof titleNode.textContent === 'string' ? titleNode.textContent.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim().slice(0, 160) : '';
watching = { cleared: false, observer: null, timer: 0 };
